We reviewed your June and July 2026 bills and the associated meter readings. The July bill is higher because the meter showed higher measured usage in July than in June.

We reviewed the June 2026 and July 2026 billing records, the actual meter reads taken on 2026-06-30 and 2026-07-31, the supplied rate components (energy charge and fixed charge), the remote meter diagnostic from 2026-07-28, and the usage history provided for recent months.

The July consumption is 240 kWh (50%) higher than June. The supplied energy rate and fixed charge reproduce the billed totals for both months. The remote diagnostic returned PASS and there are no recorded meter events in the supplied records.

Why your bill changed
The billed amount increased because measured energy use increased: July usage (720 kWh) is 240 kWh higher than June (480 kWh). Using the supplied rate (0.21 USD per kWh) and fixed charge (10.00 USD), the difference in charges equals 240 kWh × 0.21 USD/kWh = 50.40 USD, which matches the increase in the July bill.

What happens next
If you would like, we can provide guidance on checking household usage (for example, reviewing air conditioning, appliance use, or occupancy changes) and request additional documents such as a full bill line-item breakdown or a 12-month usage history for comparison. If you prefer further meter validation beyond the remote test, we can escalate to schedule a human-reviewed meter test or technician visit; that step requires human approval.

What we need from you
If you want more detail, please tell us whether you would like: (1) a full bill line-item breakdown and 12-month usage history for review, (2) guidance on checking household usage and appliances, or (3) to request a human-reviewed meter test/technician visit. If you do not request further action, no adjustment will be made because the billed amounts reconcile to the measured usage and supplied rates.
